title: I asked AI to build an entire UI with HTML/CSS. Here’s how it turned out
author: Environmental-Wear13
selftext:
After seeing the previous posts about generating entire cinematic scenes with HTML/CSS, and trying it myself, I was thinking. What if it could generate other pixelart resources as well?

It came up with an “ArtLab” to showcase the assets, before starting to reimplement the entire UI in my game with a toggle button so that I could quickly switch between the different versions. 25 minutes later I had my new UI, and honestly. I'm really thrilled with the results. But it’s also a little bittersweet, I put so many hours into my old UI so it feels a bit sad that I could make something much better in just 25 minutes.

Just wanted to share my new findings here in case someone else was interested.

comments.author: damocles_paw
comments.body: Not sure what you're saying. Is your game in, like, C#, and Claude built a HTML/CSS system into it, and also added the HTML/CSS code for a specific UI?

replies.author: Environmental-Wear13
replies.body:
Great question, I was terrible at explaining that.

No HTML renderer in the game. It's a Unity game written years ago in C# with uGUI, and HTML is only used as a drawing tool outside the engine.

Art**:** I have a small browser-based "ArtLab" where the UI sprites (panels, frames, bars, icons) are drawn pixel by pixel with JavaScript on a canvas. A script exports them as PNGs, about 130 of them for this UI.

In Unity**:** the PNGs are imported as normal sprites with 9-slice borders. The UI itself (journal, trade, dialogue and so on) is built with regular Unity UI from C# at runtime. Nothing HTML runs in the game.
